title_en: Standardization Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is formulated in order to strengthen standardization work, improve the quality of products and services, promote scientific and technological progress, ensure the safety of human health and life and property, safeguard national security and ecological environment security, and raise the level of economic and social development.

Article 2 For the purposes of this Law, "standards" (including standard samples) refer to the technical requirements that need to be unified in fields such as agriculture, industry, service industry, and social undertakings.
Standards include national standards, industry standards, local standards, group standards, and enterprise standards. National standards are divided into compulsory standards and recommended standards; industry standards and local standards are recommended standards.
Compulsory standards must be implemented. The State encourages the adoption of recommended standards.

Article 3 The tasks of standardization work are to develop standards, organize the implementation of standards, and supervise the development and implementation of standards.
People's governments at or above the county level shall incorporate standardization work into their respective national economic and social development plans, and incorporate funds for standardization work into their respective budgets.

Article 4 In developing standards, thorough investigation and demonstration shall be conducted based on the results of scientific and technological research and social practice experience, and opinions shall be widely solicited, so as to ensure the scientific nature, standardization, and timeliness of standards, and improve the quality of standards.

Article 5 The standardization administrative department of the State Council shall uniformly administer the national standardization work. The relevant administrative departments of the State Council shall, within their respective functions, administer the standardization work of their own departments and industries.
The standardization administrative departments of the local people's governments at or above the county level shall uniformly administer the standardization work within their respective administrative regions. The relevant administrative departments of the local people's governments at or above the county level shall, within their respective functions, administer the standardization work of their own departments and industries within their respective administrative regions.

Article 6 The State Council shall establish a standardization coordination mechanism to coordinate the promotion of major reforms in standardization, study major policies on standardization, and coordinate the development and implementation of standards involving cross-departments, cross-fields, or with major disputes.
Local people's governments at or above the level of a city divided into districts may, based on work needs, establish standardization coordination mechanisms to coordinate major matters of standardization work within their respective administrative regions.
Article 7 The State encourages enterprises, social organizations, and educational and scientific research institutions to carry out or participate in standardization work.

Article 8 The State shall actively promote participation in international standardization activities, conduct foreign cooperation and exchanges in standardization, participate in the development of international standards, adopt international standards in light of national conditions, and advance the transformation and application of Chinese standards and foreign standards.
The State encourages enterprises, social organizations, and educational and scientific research institutions to participate in international standardization activities.
Article 9 Units and individuals that have made remarkable achievements in standardization work shall be commended and rewarded in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State.

Article 10 Compulsory national standards shall be developed for technical requirements that ensure the safety of human health and life and property, national security, ecological environment security, and meet the basic needs of economic and social management.
The relevant administrative departments of the State Council, within their respective functions, shall be responsible for the proposal, drafting, solicitation of opinions, and technical review of compulsory national standards. The standardization administrative department of the State Council shall be responsible for the project approval, numbering, and external notification of compulsory national standards. The standardization administrative department of the State Council shall conduct project approval review on whether the proposed compulsory national standards comply with the provisions of the preceding paragraph, and shall approve the project for those that comply.
The standardization administrative departments of the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government may submit project approval suggestions for compulsory national standards to the standardization administrative department of the State Council, and the standardization administrative department of the State Council shall, together with the relevant administrative departments of the State Council, decide on the matter. Social organizations, enterprises, public institutions, and citizens may submit project approval suggestions for compulsory national standards to the standardization administrative department of the State Council; if the standardization administrative department of the State Council considers that project approval is necessary, it shall, together with the relevant administrative departments of the State Council, decide on the matter.
Compulsory national standards shall be approved and issued, or authorized to be approved and issued, by the State Council.
Where laws, administrative regulations, and decisions of the State Council provide otherwise on the development of compulsory standards, such provisions shall prevail.

Article 11 Recommended national standards may be developed for technical requirements that meet the needs of basic commonality, supporting compulsory national standards, or playing a leading role in relevant industries.
Recommended national standards shall be developed by the standardization administrative department of the State Council.

Article 12 Industry standards may be developed for technical requirements for which there is no recommended national standard and which need to be unified within a certain industry nationwide.
Industry standards shall be developed by the relevant administrative departments of the State Council and shall be submitted to the standardization administrative department of the State Council for recordation.

Article 13 Local standards may be developed to meet special technical requirements such as local natural conditions and customs.
Local standards shall be developed by the standardization administrative departments of the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the standardization administrative departments of the people's governments of cities divided into districts may, based on the special needs of their respective administrative regions and with the approval of the standardization administrative departments of the people's governments of the provinces, autonomous regions, or municipalities directly under the Central Government where they are located, develop local standards for their respective administrative regions. Local standards shall be submitted by the standardization administrative departments of the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government to the standardization administrative department of the State Council for recordation, and shall be notified by the standardization administrative department of the State Council to the relevant administrative departments of the State Council.

Article 14 For standard projects urgently needed to ensure the safety of human health and life and property, national security, ecological environment security, and economic and social development, the administrative departments responsible for developing standards shall give priority to project approval and complete them in a timely manner.

Article 15 In developing compulsory standards and recommended standards, surveys of the actual needs of relevant administrative departments, enterprises, social organizations, consumers, and educational and scientific research institutions shall be conducted at the time of project approval, and the necessity and feasibility of developing the standards shall be demonstrated and evaluated; during the development process, opinions shall be solicited through various means in accordance with the principle of convenience and effectiveness, investigations, analyses, experiments, and demonstrations of matters related to the standards shall be organized, and coordination and consistency among relevant standards shall be achieved.

Article 16 In developing recommended standards, a standardization technical committee composed of relevant parties shall be organized to undertake the drafting and technical review of the standards. In developing compulsory standards, relevant standardization technical committees may be entrusted to undertake the drafting and technical review of the standards. Where no standardization technical committee is formed, an expert group shall be established to undertake the drafting and technical review of the relevant standards. The composition of standardization technical committees and expert groups shall have broad representativeness.

Article 17 The texts of compulsory standards shall be made available to the public free of charge. The State promotes the making available of the texts of recommended standards to the public free of charge.

Article 18 The State encourages social organizations such as learned societies, associations, chambers of commerce, federations, and industrial technology alliances to coordinate relevant market entities to jointly develop group standards that meet market and innovation needs, which shall be adopted by agreement among the members of the group or made available for voluntary adoption by the public in accordance with the provisions of the group.
In developing group standards, the principles of openness, transparency, and fairness shall be followed, and the participating entities shall be ensured access to relevant information and the common needs of the participating entities shall be reflected, and investigations, analyses, experiments, and demonstrations of matters related to the standards shall be organized.
The standardization administrative department of the State Council, together with the relevant administrative departments of the State Council, shall regulate, guide, and supervise the development of group standards.
Article 19 Enterprises may, based on needs, independently develop enterprise standards, or jointly develop enterprise standards with other enterprises.

Article 20 The State supports the use of independent innovation technologies to develop group standards and enterprise standards in fields such as important industries, strategic emerging industries, and key common technologies.

Article 21 The technical requirements of recommended national standards, industry standards, local standards, group standards, and enterprise standards shall not be lower than the relevant technical requirements of compulsory national standards.
The State encourages social groups and enterprises to develop group standards and enterprise standards with technical requirements higher than those of the relevant recommended standards.

Article 22 The formulation of standards shall facilitate the scientific and rational utilization of resources, promote scientific and technological achievements, enhance the safety, universality, and interchangeability of products, and improve economic, social, and ecological benefits, so as to be technically advanced and economically reasonable.
It is prohibited to use standards to engage in acts that impede the free circulation of goods or services and that exclude or restrict market competition.

Article 23 The State promotes the civil-military integration and resource sharing of standardization, raises the level of commonality between civil and military standards, actively encourages the adoption of advanced and applicable civil standards in national defense and military construction, and converts advanced and applicable military standards into civil standards.

Article 24 Standards shall be numbered in accordance with numbering rules. The numbering rules of standards shall be formulated and published by the standardization administrative department of the State Council.
Article 25 Products and services that do not conform to compulsory standards shall not be produced, sold, imported, or provided.
Article 26 The technical requirements of exported products and services shall be implemented in accordance with the contract.

Article 27 The State implements a system for self-declaration, disclosure, and supervision of group standards and enterprise standards. An enterprise shall disclose the number and name of the compulsory standard, recommended standard, group standard, or enterprise standard that it implements; if an enterprise implements a self-developed enterprise standard, it shall also disclose the functional indicators of the products and services and the performance indicators of the products. The State encourages group standards and enterprise standards to be disclosed to the public through the standard information public service platform.
An enterprise shall organize its production and business operations in accordance with the standards, and the products it produces and the services it provides shall conform to the technical requirements of the standards it publicly discloses.
Article 28 When an enterprise develops new products, improves products, or carries out technical transformation, it shall comply with the standardization requirements set forth in this Law.

Article 29 The State establishes a system for statistical analysis and reporting on the implementation of compulsory standards.
The standardization administrative department of the State Council, the relevant administrative departments of the State Council, and the standardization administrative departments of local people's governments at or above the level of a city divided into districts shall establish a mechanism for feedback and evaluation of standard implementation information, and shall review the standards they have formulated based on the feedback and evaluation. The review period for standards shall generally not exceed five years. Upon review, standards that are no longer suitable for economic and social development needs or technological progress shall be promptly revised or abolished.

Article 30 The standardization administrative department of the State Council, based on the feedback, evaluation, and review of standard implementation, shall, for standards that are overlapping, conflicting, or inconsistent with each other, handle the matter jointly with the relevant administrative departments of the State Council or through the standardization coordination mechanism of the State Council.

Article 31 People's governments at or above the county level shall support the conduct of standardization pilot demonstration and promotional work, disseminate the concept of standardization, promote standardization experience, encourage the whole society to use standardization methods to organize production, operation, management, and services, and give full play to the supporting role of standards in promoting transformation and upgrading and leading innovation-driven development.

Article 32 The standardization administrative departments and relevant administrative departments of people's governments at or above the county level shall, within their statutory duties, provide guidance and supervision over the formulation of standards, and conduct supervision and inspection over the implementation of standards.

Article 33 Where disputes arise among the relevant administrative departments of the State Council during the formulation or implementation of standards, the standardization administrative department of the State Council shall organize consultations; if consultations fail, the matter shall be resolved by the standardization coordination mechanism of the State Council.

Article 34 Where a relevant administrative department of the State Council or a standardization administrative department of a local people's government at or above the level of a city divided into districts fails to number, review, or file a standard in accordance with this Law, the standardization administrative department of the State Council shall require it to explain the circumstances and make corrections within a specified time limit.

Article 35 Any entity or individual shall have the right to report or complain to the standardization administrative department or the relevant administrative department about any act violating the provisions of this Law.
The standardization administrative department and the relevant administrative department shall make public to the society the telephone numbers, mailboxes, or email addresses for receiving reports and complaints, and assign personnel to handle such reports and complaints. For whistleblowers or complainants who provide their real names, the administrative department receiving the report or complaint shall inform them of the handling results, keep the whistleblower's identity confidential, and give rewards to the whistleblower in accordance with relevant state regulations.

Article 36 Where products produced, sold, or imported, or services provided do not conform to compulsory standards, or where the products produced or services provided by an enterprise do not conform to the technical requirements of its publicly disclosed standards, the entity shall bear civil liability according to law.

Article 37 Where products produced, sold, or imported, or services provided do not conform to compulsory standards, the matter shall be investigated and dealt with in accordance with the Product Quality Law of the People's Republic of China, the Law of the People's Republic of China on Import and Export Commodity Inspection, the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests, and other laws and administrative regulations, the violation shall be recorded in the credit record, and shall be publicly announced in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws and administrative regulations; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 38 Where an enterprise fails to publicly disclose the standards it implements in accordance with this Law, the standardization administrative department shall order it to make corrections within a specified time limit; if it fails to make corrections within the time limit, the matter shall be publicly announced on the standard information public service platform.

Article 39 Where the standards formulated by the relevant administrative departments of the State Council or the standardization administrative departments of local people's governments at or above the level of a city divided into districts do not comply with the provisions of Paragraph 1 of Article 21 or Paragraph 1 of Article 22 of this Law, they shall promptly make corrections; if they refuse to make corrections, the standardization administrative department of the State Council shall announce the abolition of the relevant standards; the leading personnel and the directly responsible personnel shall be given sanctions according to law.
Where the standards formulated by social groups or enterprises do not comply with the provisions of Paragraph 1 of Article 21 or Paragraph 1 of Article 22 of this Law, the standardization administrative department shall order them to make corrections within a specified time limit; if they fail to make corrections within the time limit, the standardization administrative department of the people's government at or above the provincial level shall abolish the relevant standards and publicly announce them on the standard information public service platform.
Where the provisions of Paragraph 2 of Article 22 of this Law are violated by using standards to engage in acts that exclude or restrict market competition, the matter shall be dealt with in accordance with the Anti-monopoly Law of the People's Republic of China and other laws and administrative regulations.

Article 40 Where a relevant administrative department of the State Council or a standardization administrative department of a local people's government at or above the level of a city divided into districts fails to number or file a standard in accordance with this Law, and also fails to make corrections in accordance with Article 34 of this Law, the standardization administrative department of the State Council shall revoke the number of the relevant standard or announce the abolition of the un-filed standard; the leading personnel and the directly responsible personnel shall be given sanctions according to law.
Where a relevant administrative department of the State Council or a standardization administrative department of a local people's government at or above the level of a city divided into districts fails to review the standards it has formulated in accordance with this Law, and also fails to make corrections in accordance with Article 34 of this Law, the leading personnel and the directly responsible personnel shall be given sanctions according to law.

Article 41 Where the competent administrative department for standardization under the State Council fails to approve a project for developing mandatory national standards in accordance with the provisions of Article 10, paragraph 2 of this Law, the developed standards do not comply with the provisions of Article 21, paragraph 1 and Article 22, paragraph 1 of this Law, or it fails to number, review, or file the standards in accordance with the provisions of this Law, it shall promptly make corrections; the leading persons in charge and the directly responsible persons may be given sanctions according to law.

Article 42 Where a social organization or an enterprise fails to number a group standard or an enterprise standard in accordance with the provisions of this Law, the competent administrative department for standardization shall order it to make corrections within a specified time limit; if it fails to make corrections within the time limit, the competent administrative department for standardization of the people's government at or above the provincial level shall revoke the relevant standard number and make a public announcement on the standard information public service platform.

Article 43 Where a supervisor or manager of standardization work abuses his or her power, neglects his or her duty, or engages in malpractice for personal gain, he or she shall be given sanctions according to law; if the act constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.
Article 44 The measures for the development, implementation, and supervision of military standards shall be separately formulated by the State Council and the Central Military Commission.
Article 45 This Law shall come into force as of January 1, 2018.
